description: Server-scoped ModSecurity configuration, staged rules, vendor lifecycle and diagnostics. Requires the Web Server role. Payload rule text, logs, configuration and settings may contain sensitive data. Deployment may restart Apache; API outcomes and per-item results remain distinct.

notes.text: Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.
Adds only to the staging file; deployAllRuleChanges() is a separate operation. The source leaves config, config_active, staged, vendor_active and vendor_id unconstrained; their values remain mixed.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.
The server obtains vendor metadata and a compatible rule archive from the supplied URL. This can fetch remote content and install a rule set; a successful call does not establish rule enforcement.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.48 and later.
For a single upload, set both init and final. Omitted flags retain server defaults; deploy=false stages without deployment. This call can deploy configuration when deploy=true.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.

The typed signature supports a single setting. Indexed setting_id1/state1/remove1 families remain unavailable through this signature (whm-api-client-8x0.1.24). remove=true makes the state value ignored by the server, but the formal source still requires state. State can contain a SecHttpBlKey access key and is sensitive.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.
POST follows the pinned x-readonly=false declaration. API success only confirms the check ran; inspect valid and optional problem to decide whether the rule passed validation.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.48 and later.
Creates a copy with a new rule ID. This method accepts an integer ID; disableRule() and undisableRule() instead retain their documented string IDs.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.48 and later.
Can restart Apache. Inspect every outcomes[].ok and the optional failed list independently of API success; failed validation restores the original configuration and preserves staged changes.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.
Can restart Apache. Failed validation restores the original configuration and keeps staged changes. The source declares an unconstrained data node, which remains mixed; an absent payload is distinct.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.48 and later.

Deploys settings prepared with setSetting() and attempts to restart Apache. Failed validation restores the settings file. The source does not define payload fields; an absent payload remains a mismatch.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.
The ID remains a string as documented, including leading zeros; this differs from the integer identifiers accepted by cloneRule(), editRule() and removeRule(). The source documents no data payload.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.48 and later.
Individually enabled configuration files remain enabled. The empty source data schema remains mixed rather than inventing fields or requiring an object.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.48 and later.
Inspect outcomes[].active and outcomes[].ok and any exception for each file; API success alone does not establish that every configuration was disabled.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.48 and later.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.48 and later.
Discards staged changes for all configuration files. Inspect per-file outcomes[].ok and the optional failed list independently of API success.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.
Deletes the selected configuration staging file, losing its staged changes. The empty source data schema remains unconstrained.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.
Writes edits to the staging file only; deployment is a separate operation. Its integer ID contract differs from disableRule() and undisableRule().
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.48 and later.
Individually disabled configuration files remain disabled. Enabling the vendor does not establish effective request blocking.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.48 and later.
Inspect per-file outcomes[].active, outcomes[].ok and optional exception independently of the API result.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.48 and later.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.
Returned configuration text may contain secrets. Treat it as sensitive payload data and avoid logging it.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.48 and later.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.

Log content may contain request data, IP addresses and sensitive transaction fragments. Keep nullable fields distinct from omission; timezone is an integer here, unlike the string timezone in reportRule() hits.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.48 and later.
Supply config or vendorId as required by the source prose; both formal parameters remain optional to preserve the selector alternatives. Rule text and metadata may contain sensitive data.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.
Setting state can contain a SecHttpBlKey access key. Treat settings and validator data as sensitive payloads; returned validators describe frontend checks, not proof that current settings are secure.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.
Returns metadata only; the client does not fetch returned archive, report or vendor URLs. Installation, update and in-use fields describe different states.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.
The installed flag is nested under data in the API data payload. An installed module does not establish that rules are active or blocking requests.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.
Adds a configuration include. The client does not retry or undo the change; API success does not establish request filtering behavior.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.
Removes a configuration include. The client does not retry or undo the change.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.48 and later.
POST follows the pinned x-readonly=false declaration even though this returns metadata. The supplied metadata URL can cause a server-side fetch; this is not a local parse.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.
Removes the selected rule using the source integer ID contract. No client retry or rollback is provided.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.48 and later.
Removes the vendor includes, disablement directives, configuration files and metadata file. The source documents no data payload.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.48 and later.

send=true submits event data, message and contact email to a remote receiver; send=false prepares the report without sending. The formal row_ids schema is integer despite comma-separated multi-ID prose and examples, so this typed method accepts one row ID only (whm-api-client-8x0.1.24). Report content may contain sensitive request data. Report hits preserve their string timezone and nullable message separately from getLog().

evidence.note: Pinned WHM source SHA256 6edb13c51d53f3c2be1fa83cc93e31d3a81f4f8506b3b45284fa00b986041594, /modsec_report_rule response data.report explicitly says an array of objects and declares items with these fields, but omits type: array. Restore the evidenced list shape without changing item requiredness or nullable leaves.

notes.text: Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.
Stages the supplied contents; deployRuleChanges() is a separate operation. The source data schema is unconstrained and remains mixed, preserving explicit null separately from an absent payload.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.

Prepares settings for deploySettingsChanges(); changing state is not evidence of deployed enforcement. State can contain a SecHttpBlKey access key and is sensitive. The response state is documented as integer even though the input is string; validation arg and name are unconstrained in this response.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.46 and later.
Enables the selected rule using the documented string ID contract. The source documents no data payload.
Available in cPanel & WHM 11.48 and later.
The server obtains current vendor metadata and rules from the supplied URL. Inspect diagnostics and vendor state separately; API success does not establish enforcement.
